subject.title: fix(agents): prevent recursive task execution during model fallback

question: Should this PR land as a scoped embedded sessions_spawn mitigation while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92271 tracks the remaining gateway, sessions_send/cron, and Codex-native spawn surfaces, or should it wait for one shared work-spawning policy seam?
rationale: The patch appears correct for the embedded choke point, but it deliberately chooses a partial fail-closed boundary and leaves related delegation surfaces uncovered; automation should not decide that product and ownership boundary.

options.title: Accept Scoped Mitigation After Rebase
options.body: Resolve the current merge conflict, land the embedded guard, and keep the umbrella issue open for the remaining surfaces.

options.title: Require Shared Policy First
options.body: Hold this PR until one maintainer-approved work-spawning policy seam covers OpenClaw tools and Codex-native delegation consistently.

options.title: Split Owned Follow-Ups First
options.body: Pause merge until maintainers create or assign explicit follow-up owners for gateway loopback, sessions_send/cron, and Codex-native spawn.

recommendation.title: Accept Scoped Mitigation After Rebase
recommendation.body: Resolve the current merge conflict, land the embedded guard, and keep the umbrella issue open for the remaining surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is assigned and authored the cross-harness review that defined the unresolved scope decision.
